cards.text: Isaiah, a prophet, has a message, and this one covers the WHOLE earth. Isaiah says, "Behold, the LORD lays waste the earth and leaves it in ruins." He'll twist its surface and scatter everybody who lives on it.

cards.question: As the LORD scatters the earth's people, Isaiah names priest and people, master and servant, lender and borrower. How does the scattering fall on them?

answers.text: On every one of them alike
On the servants more than the masters
On the borrowers but not the lenders

cards.text: Alike. The whole list, top to bottom, and it's like a blackout on the whole block, baker: the boss's fridge goes dark same as yours, fancy ice maker and all.

cards.question: Isaiah says the earth will be utterly laid waste and thoroughly plundered. True or false: He says this is only his own guess.

cards.text: The earth mourns and withers, the world fades, and even the exalted of the earth waste away. Turns out the VIPs don't get a VIP exit.

cards.question: Isaiah says the earth is defiled by its people. They have transgressed the laws and overstepped the decrees. What else have they broken?
Isaiah says a curse has consumed the earth, and its people must bear the guilt. True or false: He says everyone on the earth survives.

cards.text: The earth's dwellers have been burned, and only a few survive. Then Isaiah turns to the vine.

cards.question: The new wine dries up and the vine withers. What happens to all the merrymakers?

cards.text: Tambourines, revelers, harp: all gone quiet, and friend, I KNOW that kind of quiet. In my old junk drawer, a rubber band snapping was the big news for a WEEK.

cards.question: The people no longer sing and drink wine. Strong drink is ___ to those who consume it.

cards.text: Then Isaiah turns to a city he calls the city of chaos. It's shattered, and every house is closed to entry.

cards.question: In the streets of the city of chaos, they cry out for wine. All joy turns to ___.
True or false: When the city of chaos is left in ruins, its gate is still standing strong.

cards.text: Isaiah says it will be like this on the earth and among the nations. Then he reaches for a picture from harvest time.

cards.question: Isaiah compares the earth and the nations to an olive tree after the harvest and a vine after the grapes are gathered. What does that picture show?

cards.text: Then the sound changes, baker, and voices go up, shouting for joy. From the west, they proclaim the majesty of the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: The only praise for the LORD anyone hears is coming from the west.

cards.text: There's a call to glorify the LORD in the east and in the islands of the sea, and from the ends of the earth there's singing: "Glory to the Righteous One." It's the world's biggest group chat, and for once EVERYBODY replies.

cards.question: The ends of the earth are singing glory to the Righteous One. Then the prophet cuts in with a but. What does he say?

cards.text: The prophet says, "I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Woe is me." And the next line: "The treacherous betray; the treacherous deal in treachery."
Then the message turns to whoever lives on the earth. Terror and pit and snare are waiting.

cards.question: Terror and pit and snare are waiting for the earth's people. Someone flees the sound of panic. Where do they end up?

answers.text: They reach a city of refuge

cards.question: True or false: Whoever climbs out of the pit is finally safe.

cards.text: Out of the panic, into the pit, and out of the pit, into the snare. It's like finally getting out of rush hour just to hit every red light in town.
Isaiah says, "For the windows of heaven are open, and the foundations of the earth are shaken." The earth is broken apart, split open and shaken violently.

cards.question: The earth is breaking apart and shaking violently. Isaiah says it staggers like what?
The earth staggers like a drunkard and sways like a shack. Earth's ___ weighs it down, and it falls, never to rise again.

cards.text: Then Isaiah looks ahead to that day. He sees what's coming, both up above and down below.

cards.question: In that day the LORD will punish the host of ___ above and the kings of the ___ below.

cards.text: They'll be gathered together like prisoners in a pit, confined to a dungeon and punished after many days. And I used to think my junk drawer was a tight squeeze.

cards.question: Isaiah says the moon will be confounded and the sun will be ashamed. Why?

answers.text: The LORD of Hosts will reign

cards.question: True or false: Isaiah says the LORD of Hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem.

cards.text: He'll reign there before His elders, with great glory. The sun and moon are the brightest lights we've got, baker, and next to Him, they're ashamed.

findings.problem: The setup says the LORD will 'scatter everybody who lives on it.' That rules out card 2's wrong answer 'On the borrowers but not the lenders' before the baker gets to choose, because 'everybody' already includes the lenders.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the answer to card 2 ('Alike. The whole list, top to bottom') and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap card. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. ... Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: 'What does he say?' asks the baker to guess the prophet's next words ('I am wasting away' against 'I have seen enough'). Both plausible answers fit the 'but,' so the pick comes down to luck. The question should ask about the meaning, such as how the prophet reacts to the singing.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says. Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'Out of the panic, into the pit, and out of the pit, into the snare' only restates the answers to cards 7 and 8, then adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. ... Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: 'next to Him, they're ashamed' says the sun and the moon are both ashamed. Isaiah 24:23 says the moon will be confounded and the sun will be ashamed.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
